slides.heading: Largest Park
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Stacks
slides.narration: Let's solve Largest Park, a very hard stacks problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Boolean matrix where false is free land and true is in use.
Area of the largest all-free rectangle (0 if none).
For each row build a histogram of consecutive free cells above and take the largest rectangle in it with a monotonic stack.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Boolean matrix where false is free land and true is in use. Area of the largest all-free rectangle (0 if none). For each row build a histogram of consecutive free cells above and take the largest rectangle in it with a monotonic stack.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Treat each row as a histogram of free heights and apply the largest rectangle in histogram.
slides.narration: Treat each row as a histogram of free heights and apply the largest rectangle in histogram.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Histogram per row + monotonic stack → O(R·C)
slides.narration: Checking every rectangle is huge. Treating each row as the base of a histogram and using the skyline stack is linear in the grid.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, update column heights per row. Second, run the monotonic stack. Third, track the max area.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of w times h. Space is O of w.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: A blocked cell resets that column's height to zero.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Treat each row as a histogram of free heights and apply the largest rectangle in histogram.
